reviews.review:
Note: I originally played this game on my PS4 when it originally released, hence the low Steam hours. I bought it again to give it another shot.

[h1][b]Grey Area[/b][/h1]
    I love Mass Effect as a game series, an idea, and as a book series. The original trilogy of games was something I loved playing as they released, and I even went to ME3's midnight release. I was excited when Andromeda got announced, as the idea of exploring another galaxy was amazing, and opened up the possibility of meeting new species for the first time, and having those moments feel great similar to how they did in the first game. Then... it came out.

[h2][b]Gameplay[/b][/h2]
Honestly, the gameplay is probably the best part of the game. The movement system is light years better than the original trilogy, and the gun-play feels great too. However, that's about where the positives end for me with the gameplay. When you're not shooting at Kett, you're going to have to travel from place to place on a planet to find more to shoot at. However, due to the emptiness of most of the planets, this is a chore from start to finish.

It is truly insane how most of these planets have nothing to do, or to look at. On most planets there is a main settlement area, and then Remnant ruins scattered about. Obviously, the trilogy was much more linear, and the parts that had driving were just as empty. However, those games did not market themselves as "Open World" like Andromeda does. Usually, in said Open World, you should have some level of random encounters beyond Kett dropping in on your head, or the occasional mining node to send out.

Also, the crew in Andromeda is just... lacking. Vetra is about the only standout among all of them, and I like Nakmor Drack simply because he reminds me of Wrex and Grunt from the Trilogy. Cora and Liam are the base human crew members that add nothing, and Peebee is just... Peebee? She's around, and she's the Remnant Expert in the same way that Liara was the expert on Reapers. Then, there's Jaal, and the rest of the Angara.

[h2][b]World Building[/b][/h2]
While Jaal has his moments, it is quickly apparent his only role is to fill the shoes of Javik from ME3. And that's fine, each squadmate is supposed to remind you of someone from the originals... I think? But Jaal himself isn't the main problem here. It's the Angara as a whole.

You're telling me that we went to a completely new Galaxy, and we only managed to meet a single new species? I don't count the Kett due to [spoiler]them literally just being transformed Angarans[/spoiler], so that just leaves us with a single new species in the whole galaxy. In the Milky Way alone (according to a full breakdown on the wiki), there were 29 different races, not counting non-sapients such as Pyjaks, Klixen, those kinda things. 

I just feel like Bioware dropped the ball with the whole "We're going to a new galaxy" idea with just introducing the Angarans as the only completely new race in the game. 

[h2][b]Story[/b][/h2]
The story is... fine? If you completely ignore what came before this game, then it's a decent enough story. Ryder, at least the male version as that is who I selected, is probably the most boring, uninteresting, and borderline unlikeable character Bioware could've given us. Shepherd worked because Bioware doubled down on his dry voice acting and dry jokes, whereas it feels like they genuinely tried making Ryder likeable, and it just missed the mark by... a couple football fields imo. 

The beginning of the story is entirely predictable, which, fine. At this point I've played enough games in my life, that I'm used to just guessing who is going to die, and what is going to happen. However, certain things are handled in such a way that there is nothing in this game that shocks me at any point in the story. Even [spoiler]the reveal with the Kett/Angaran thing[/spoiler] didn't catch me *super* off guard. Just enough for me to go, "Oh, okay. Well I guess that makes sense but not really?" The ending also leaves much to be desired, and leaves too many questions for a sequel that will never come. Too many things were set up to be explored/answered in a sequel, and with ME5 going back to the Milky Way, it seems we'll never get answers or expansion.

[h2][b]Overall[/b][/h2]
ME:A is... a game. It's a sci-fi/action/3PS game. If you separate it from the original trilogy, and ignore the easter eggs thrown in there [spoiler]with Garrus and Liara cameos[/spoiler], then it's not a horrible game. However, if you go in expecting it to live up to ME1-ME3, then prepare to be wildly, and aggressively disappointed. Andromeda as just Andromeda, is a fine game. However, as Mass Effect: Andromeda, it's comically bad.

Only buy this game on a good discount. There will never be a sequel/followup game for this. Effectively, this is a one-shot game that could be skipped, and you probably won't even hear a single thing about it beyond "We sent colonists to another galaxy" in ME5.
fun gameplay and lots of it. This is no done in a weekend type deal.
